reason: Episode shows a 330-error downstream engine build triaged into error classes, reduced to generic repros, and routed to numeric, resolver, and interpreter streams instead of hand-editing source. No index skill covers this method; wj-repro covers only a single failure.

A downstream build (wj-game) failed with a single E0425 inside compiler source, so this skill's "many errors" trigger missed it. The right move was to trace the symbol through git history and restore it on the integration branch, not to build the downstream against an old git archive snapshot. Adds that class to the triage and broadens the trigger.

Add the class where the error is a missing symbol inside the compiler itself: that is a broken integration HEAD, traced via git history and fixed at the source, with a pointer to the merge-verification skill.

Mid-episode the integrator told the downstream game agent to stop using a pinned snapshot now that the integration HEAD builds, and to re-run from a fresh build with a per-class error report versus the 330-error baseline. The triage skill forbids snapshot workarounds but does not say how to re-verify after the fix lands; this adds that step.

The old line said a rising total is never a regression by itself. This episode had a real regression: a default type for untyped integers was applied without unifying with typed operands, and a two-line repro showed it. The rule needs to separate masked-error exposure from a change that breaks something that compiled before.
Gives the owner-routing step a concrete numeric rule, so the next width regression is routed to unification rather than patched in codegen.
